fixture.limitation: Provisional until the first real save. This world is synthetic: it exercises the shape of a save (terrain, caves, overhangs, structures and mixed materials) but was not produced by gameplay, by docs/worldgen-design.md, or by the save path on the reference machine. Its byte sizes, material histograms and distributions are illustrative only and must not be quoted as gate results (M1-35, M1-37) until a real save is captured and this fixture is re-frozen.

rows.pre_registered: 40% of 8,188 MiB = 3,275 MiB; hard fail at 60% = 4,913 MiB
rows.note: Projected from the measured p95 total per chunk; the max chunk (1.03 MiB) would project to 25.84 GiB. The target row is 3.20 GiB (-21.56 GiB), the hard-fail row is 4.80 GiB (-19.96 GiB). The gate uses p95 by pre-registration, not the mean, and does not apply the 1.5× factor a second time.

rows.pre_registered: Per profile and edge, table §2: N64 = 25,736, N128 = 3,216
rows.measured: N64 = 25,736 at 64³; N128 = 3,217 at 128³ equal volume
rows.note: The gate asserts the frozen model's equal-volume identity, N64 = 8 × N128. The table's own N64/N128 are a prediction: measured 25,736 / 3,217 against 25,736 / 3,216 (deltas 0 / +1). Those deltas are the table's nearest-integer rounding and are reported, not folded back into the model. N64 feeds the memory projection.

The node count is the banded internal-node arena (`dag_node_bytes / 8`), so it is a hard per-chunk cap, not a p95. The other edge's budget is pre-registered but not measured by this build; M1-40 supplies the 128³ projection before M1-42.
One 16 B cell per block, fixed by the compiled chunk edge. The 128³ value is the frozen pre-registration target and is not built in M1.
One 12 B SH4 RGB probe per block at the near LOD. The update row measures the latency; this row checks both the fixed grid and the byte volume. The 128³ value is pre-registered, not built in M1.

rows.measured: p95 753 KiB (max 775 KiB); greedy estimate × 76 B
rows.note: The estimate is greedy quads × 76 B and excludes vertex/index buffer overhead. The predicted lower bound is 150 KiB; a lower estimate is not a failure, but it is not a measured GPU buffer either. The gate uses p95 and reports max separately.

rows.pre_registered: p95 ≤ 8 ms (consolidate + upload + fence + flip + dirty light)
rows.note: Fixed = upload + fence + flip; dirty = COW + light. The fence and upload are the CPU side of the M4 protocol; the headless gate has no GPU device time, so this is a lower bound on a real device path, not a claim about GPU completion.

rows.measured: p95 143.351 µs (p50 54.303 µs, max 288.318 µs); 1,000 edited chunks
rows.note: Update = select + rebake + upload. Only probes whose rays reach the dirty voxel are rebaked; the upload is the CPU staging copy and excludes the device transfer and the M4 fence/flip.

rows.pre_registered: ≤ 15% traversed-but-invisible at chunk boundaries @ max view
rows.source: M1-34 reference; no archived gate result
rows.note: The reference instrumentation and its 100-pose test exist, but this generator consumes M1-35…M1-38 only. A granularity run must be attached before M1-41, or this row keeps the gate incomplete; it is not silently passed.

This is an invariant on the frozen budget, not a second measurement. The factor survives hardware changes because the fraction (40%/60%) does; applying it twice would make the gate stricter than the pre-registration.

rows.pre_registered: Real populated save; median, p95, max per chunk
rows.note: Provisional until the first real save. This world is synthetic: it exercises the shape of a save (terrain, caves, overhangs, structures and mixed materials) but was not produced by gameplay, by docs/worldgen-design.md, or by the save path on the reference machine. Its byte sizes, material histograms and distributions are illustrative only and must not be quoted as gate results (M1-35, M1-37) until a real save is captured and this fixture is re-frozen. The distributions are measured (p50/p95/max per chunk), but the dataset is not admissible as the M1 gate result until a real populated save replaces it.

rows.pre_registered: See §4; pre-registered; no renegotiation inside M1
rows.measured: rule 2 triggered by the measured rows
rows.note: Rule 2: a voxel-memory row failed at 64³. Do not automatically stay at 64³. Run the M1-40 analytic 128³ projection; if 128³ clears, the failure is an argument for the upgrade, not against it.

fallback.action: Rule 2: a voxel-memory row failed at 64³. Do not automatically stay at 64³. Run the M1-40 analytic 128³ projection; if 128³ clears, the failure is an argument for the upgrade, not against it.

notes: The twelve rows are the frozen table in docs/pre-registration.md §3. Every verdict is computed from a measured value and its limit; no row is typed PASS. A row the M1-35…M1-38 harnesses do not measure is NOT MEASURED, not green.

The memory projection is the measured p95 per-chunk total multiplied by the loaded chunk count at the edge this build uses. It applies the frozen 60% hard-fail line (4,913 MiB); the 1.5× safety factor is already inside that line, so it is not applied twice.
The headless gate does not open a wgpu adapter. GPU identity is quoted from docs/reference-machine.md and is not re-probed; the host CPU, OS and architecture are read from the running process.

The fixture is provisional until the first real save. Its distributions are a rehearsal for the gate and must not be quoted as the M1 result; the dataset row stays not measured until a real save replaces it.
Culling granularity has the M1-34 reference and its 100-pose test, but this generator consumes M1-35…M1-38 only. Attach a granularity run before M1-41 or that row keeps the gate incomplete.
The fallback is computed from the measured rows with the pre-registration §4 order. It is a preview for M1-42, not a renegotiation of any threshold.
